Render determinism reproducer

This page exists to be photographed twice. It declares the same font stack the render recipe pins, so pinning it cannot change the document height. Nothing is forced to reflow, and so nothing makes the shutter wait for the injection to finish painting. The controls further down are what still change under the pin, which is the other half of the defect.

Why the height must not move

A page that gains or loses height when the font is pinned forces a layout pass, and the capture rides along behind it. That page looks deterministic while the underlying race is untouched. The bug only shows itself where the injection changes pixels without changing the box model.

Why something must still move

A page where the pin changes nothing at all is equally useless as a control: both captures are identical whichever side of the injection they land on, so the race has nothing to express itself through. Form controls and monospace elements do not inherit the body font, so they are restyled by the pin while occupying the same space.

Inline monospace behaves the same way: design-render.sh writes screenshot_sha256 into renders/<slug>.json, and every one of those code runs is restyled by the pin without moving the paragraph.

Content below the fold

The remaining paragraphs push the document past a single viewport so a full-page capture has to stitch more than one screen. Judging what sits above the fold is a separate question that belongs to a declared platform contract, not to a side effect of how the screenshot was taken.

Every line here is static. There is no script on this page, no date, no random source, no remote asset and no web font. Any difference between two consecutive captures comes from the capture, never from the page — which is the whole reason it is committed rather than generated.

Keep this file boring. If it grows a script, an image or a font link it stops being a control and starts being another variable, and the case that renders it stops proving anything about the renderer.

A green result on this page is still weak evidence on its own. The flip it reproduces was intermittent — roughly one render in four to one in ten — so a handful of agreeing captures is a smoke check, not a gate. The faked-transport cases carry the guard; this page exists so that the one real-browser case is at least pointed at a page where the defect can occur.

The last thing worth recording: the reason a page like this is hard to write is that the two requirements pull against each other. Anything that changes enough to move pixels usually also changes enough to move layout, and layout movement is precisely what hides the race. Controls are the narrow case where the first happens without the second.
